newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-FERENCVAROS OVERCOME NEWCASTLE IN FIVE-GOAL FEAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERENCVAROS OVERCOME NEWCASTLE IN FIVE-GOAL FEAST.

text.p: Hungarian champions Ferencvaros shook English title leaders Newcastle with a 3-2 UEFA Cup win on Tuesday.
Newcastle's propensity for defensive errors quickly became apparent as they found themselves two goals down with only 17 minutes of the second round, first leg gone.
A weak back pass by Belgian defender Phillipe Albert let in Ferenc Horvath for the opening goal in the seventh minute.
Just 10 minutes later Horvath headed against a post and Krisztian Lisztes was on hand to strike home the rebound.
Newcastle dug deep into their reserves and staged a brilliant recovery, with strike pair Les Ferdinand and Alan Shearer putting them level before halftime.
Ferdinand headed in from close range on 25 minutes after a textbook cross from Shearer. In-form England marksman Shearer volleyed home the equaliser in the 35th minute.
But Ferencvaros were not finished and set up an intriguing return leg in two weeks when Lisztes pounced on a misdirected clearance by Peter Beardsley and fired in a 57th minute winner.
